info.title: New Voting System
info.description: API of the New Voting System. Conventions: docs/api/README.md.

post.description:
The invited person chooses a name and a password and gets an account in the institution
that invited them, verified, with the invited role, and is signed in (the session id is
regenerated). An unknown, used or cancelled token is 404; an expired one is 410; the order
of the checks is in the endpoint file. Public. Limited to 10 requests per hour per IP address.

get.description:
The entries of the institution, newest first, 50 per page (1 to 100). Filters: `action` (a code, or a
family prefix ending with a dot), `election`, `user` (a uuid, or `system` for the scheduler), `from` and
`to` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, UTC, inclusive); one that names nothing gives an empty list. Entries of other
institutions and of the platform never appear. Owner only. The shared API limit.

An Excel or CSV file of the entries the same filters select, newest first, at most 10 000, written as a
stream: date (UTC), action code, person, election, subject, details as compact JSON, address. Every text
cell is guarded against formulas. Owner only. Limited to 20 requests per hour per user.

In display order (position, then creation), in any status of the election. An election
holds at most 50, so `per_page=100` returns them all. Owner or manager.
get.summary: List the ballots of an election

post.description:
At the end of a draft election, at most 50 per election (409 `ballot_limit_reached`).
Owner or manager. Limited to 120 requests per hour per user.

put.description:
`ballots` must be exactly the UUIDs of the election's ballots, each once, in the wanted
order (422 `ballots: set_mismatch` otherwise). A draft election only. Answers the list,
in the new order. Owner or manager. Limited to 240 requests per hour per user.

patch.description:
Every field is optional; only those sent change. Not the position (see the order
endpoint). A draft election only. Owner or manager. Limited to 120 requests per hour per user.

delete.description:
A draft election only. The positions after it close the gap. Owner or manager. Limited
to 120 requests per hour per user.

post.description:
At the end of a ballot of a draft election, at most 50 per ballot (409
`candidate_limit_reached`). The party, when given, is one of the same election. Owner or
manager. Limited to 120 requests per hour per user.

put.description:
`candidates` must be exactly the UUIDs of the ballot's candidates, each once, in the
wanted order (422 `candidates: set_mismatch` otherwise). A draft election only. Answers
the candidates, in the new order. Owner or manager. Limited to 240 requests per hour per user.
put.summary: Put the candidates of a ballot in order

patch.description:
Every field is optional; only those sent change. `ballot` moves it to the end of another
ballot of the same election. Not the position (see the order endpoint) nor the photo. A
draft election only. Owner or manager. Limited to 120 requests per hour per user.

delete.description:
A draft election only. The positions after it close the gap. Owner or manager. Limited to
120 requests per hour per user.

put.description:
Send one `file` part (`multipart/form-data`) under the rules of the election cover: JPEG,
PNG or WebP recognised by content, 5 MB, 8 000 pixels on a side, 40 million pixels, not
animated. Two WebP files are written, 160 and 480 pixels wide, ratio kept, never enlarged,
metadata dropped, the upload never kept; the previous photo's files are deleted afterwards.
A draft election only. Owner or manager. Limited to 20 requests per hour per user.
put.summary: Replace the photo of a candidate

delete.description:
Answers 204 whether or not there was a photo. A draft election only. Owner or manager.
Limited to 120 requests per hour per user.
delete.summary: Remove the photo of a candidate

put.description:
Send one `file` part (`multipart/form-data`) under the rules of the institution's logo: JPEG,
PNG or WebP recognised by content, 5 MB, 8 000 pixels on a side, 40 million pixels, not animated.
Two WebP files are written, 480 and 960 pixels wide, ratio kept, never enlarged, metadata
dropped, the upload never kept; the previous cover's files are deleted afterwards. A draft only.
Owner or manager. Limited to 20 requests per hour per user.
put.summary: Replace the cover of an election

delete.description: Answers 204 whether or not there was a cover. A draft only. Owner or manager.
delete.summary: Remove the cover of an election

post.description:
What a run would do for a scope (`all`, one `group`, `ungrouped` or `failed_email`), without
doing it: voters who would get a code, those with an email address, those with none (left
for print, the first 100 named by name) and those who already have a code. The numbers the
person confirms before emails are sent; the run checks them again. A draft, scheduled or
open election (409 `election_codes_locked`). Owner or manager. Limited to 120 requests per
hour per user.
post.summary: Preview a run of access codes

post.description:
Gives a code to the voters of the scope (`all`, one `group`, `ungrouped`, or `failed_email`
for a new code to the voters whose email failed) who have none and writes their slips, one
PDF per group (parts of 1 000 voters at most). With `email` the voters served who have an
address are emailed their link and code in the background; `confirm_emails` is the count the
person saw (409 `email_count_changed` with `error.count`, 409 `nothing_to_email`); with `email` the user's
own email must be verified (403 `email_not_verified`) and the institution's emails of the last 24
hours are limited (409 `email_quota_exceeded`, `error.count` is the number left). `file` is
`xlsx`, `csv` or null. The answer comes before the work: the files are `queued`, and polled
with `GET /generated-files/{file}`. A draft, scheduled or open election (409
`election_codes_locked`), one run at a time (409 `run_in_progress`), something to serve (409
`nothing_to_generate`). Owner or manager. Limited to 20 requests per hour per user.
post.summary: Start a run of access codes

get.description:
Totals and one line per group (sorted by name, accents and case ignored; the voters with no
group last, with a null `id` and `name`): voters, voters with a code, with an email, and
the files ready, and the emails queued, sent and failed. `run_in_progress` is true while a
file or an email is queued. Any status of the
election; once it is closed no file counts as ready. Owner or manager.
get.summary: The state of the access codes of an election

get.description:
Starts the browser's session if it has none and sets the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie. The web
application calls it once before its first state-changing request, then copies the
cookie's value into the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header of every request that changes something.
Public. Limited to 60 requests per minute per IP address.
get.summary: Start the session and set the CSRF cookie

get.description:
The institution's elections counted by status, the voters of all of them, the open elections
with their live turnout (at most 10, newest first; an election past its end is not listed),
the scheduled ones with their start, and the to-do items (`voters_not_voted`,
`draft_blockers`, `codes_missing`) with the election each concerns. No vote count of any
ballot. Owner or manager.

The elections of the signed-in user's institution as cards, archived ones left out unless
`status=archived`. Order: open, scheduled, draft, closed, published, archived; then the latest
start, then the latest created. `meta.counts` (one per status, and `all` without the archived)
and `meta.years` (newest first, read in each election's time zone) ignore the filters. Owner or manager.

post.description:
Always a draft of the caller's institution. The time zone and the language default from the
institution. A start in the past is accepted. Owner or manager. Limited to 60 requests per
hour per user.

get.description: One election of the institution, in any status. Owner or manager.

patch.description:
Every field is optional; only those sent change. The end is checked against the start as
they will be after the change. A draft only (409 `election_not_editable` otherwise). Owner or
manager. Limited to 120 requests per hour per user.

delete.description:
A draft only. The row and its cover files go for good. Owner or manager. Limited to 60
requests per hour per user.

post.description:
A new draft with the settings of this one, whatever its status: description, dates, time
zone, language, candidate order, results display. Not the cover, the status dates or the
link to a first round. The title defaults to "Copie de …" ("Copy of …" for an English
election), cut to 200 characters. Ballots and parties come with it, and the candidates when
`copy_candidates` is true. Owner or manager. Limited to 60 requests per hour per user.

get.description:
What stops the election from being scheduled (`blockers`) and what to look at first
(`warnings`), in any status. `can_schedule` is true for a draft with no blocker. Owner or
manager.

post.description:
A draft becomes scheduled: ballots, candidates and parties are locked; voters and groups stay
editable. 409 `checklist_blocked` with the blockers in `error.items`; 409 `checklist_warnings`
with the warnings unless `accept_warnings` is true; 409 `election_period_over` when the end is
not in the future. The checklist is computed again under the row lock. Owner or manager.
Limited to 120 requests per hour per user.

A scheduled election goes back to draft, so ballots and candidates can be edited again.
Voters, groups and the groups of the ballots are not touched. Owner or manager. Limited to
120 requests per hour per user. 409 `election_started` when the start has passed.

An open election is closed before its end, for good. `confirmation` must be the election's
title (case and surrounding spaces ignored, accents counted): 422 `confirmation: mismatch`.
409 `election_not_open` for any other status. The status is read again under the row lock.
Nothing about votes is read or written. Owner or manager. Limited to 20 requests per hour
per user, shared with extend.

Moves the end of a scheduled or open election later; the status stays. The new end must be
after the current one (422 `ends_at: not_after`) and at most 30 days after it (`too_far`).
409 `election_not_extendable` for another status, or when the end has passed. Owner or
manager. Limited to 20 requests per hour per user, shared with close.

Sends a reset link to the address, if it belongs to an account. The answer is the same
either way, so the endpoint does not tell whether an account exists. Public. Limited
to 5 requests per hour per IP address, and 3 per hour per email address.
post.summary: Ask for a password reset link

get.description:
The slip PDFs, newest first, ties by group name then part (the voters with no group last).
Empty once the election is closed, published or archived: the files are deleted at the end.
Owner or manager.
get.summary: List the files of an election

get.description:
For polling after a run: `queued`, `ready` (with `size_bytes`) or `failed` (`failure`
`generation_failed`). Owner or manager.

The PDF of slips (`coupons-{group}.pdf`), or the Excel or CSV file of codes (`codes-{group}.xlsx`,
`codes-tous.csv`), decrypted on the way out, with a fixed name, never cached.
409 `file_not_ready` for a queued or failed file; 404 once the election is closed,
published or archived. Owner or manager. Limited to 120 requests per hour per user.

By name, ignoring case, then creation order, with their voter counts, in any status of the
election. An election holds at most 100, so `per_page=100` returns them all. `meta` also
carries `voters_total` and `ungrouped`. Owner or manager.
get.summary: List the groups of an election

post.description:
To a draft or scheduled election, at most 100 per election (409 `group_limit_reached`).
The name is unique in the election, ignoring case and surrounding spaces. Owner or
manager. Limited to 120 requests per hour per user.

patch.description:
A draft or scheduled election only; its voters follow it. Owner or manager. Limited to
120 requests per hour per user.

delete.description:
A draft or scheduled election only, and only a group with no voter and no ballot (409 `group_in_use`).
Final: there is no trash. Owner or manager. Limited to 120 requests per hour per user.

post.description:
Every voter of the group moves to `into`, another group of the same election, and the
group is deleted, and the ballots that covered it cover `into`: one transaction. A draft or scheduled election only. Answers the
receiving group. Owner or manager. Limited to 120 requests per hour per user.

get.description:
Says whether the database and Redis answer, and returns the database server's clock.
Public. Limited to 60 requests per minute per IP address.
get.summary: State of the API and of the services it depends on

get.description:
The profile of the signed-in user's own institution; there is no way to name another. An
owner or a manager may read it. A platform admin has no institution: 403. Signed-in user.

patch.description:
Every field is optional; only those sent change. Strings are trimmed, and an optional field
sent empty is cleared. The suspension and the logo cannot be reached from here. Owner only.

get.description: Live and expired ones, newest first. The token is never returned. Owner only.
get.summary: The invitations that have not been accepted

post.description:
Invites an address to join the institution as owner or manager, and sends the email in the
institution's language. A live invitation for the same address is replaced: its link stops
working. Owner only. Limited to 20 requests per hour per user.

delete.description:
Its link stops working; the row is deleted. An invitation that is unknown, already
accepted, already cancelled or another institution's answers 404. Owner only.

post.description:
Signs a user in with email and password. The session id is regenerated. A platform
admin signs in here too. A user with two-factor authentication is not signed in yet: the
answer is `{"data":{"two_factor_required":true}}` and the sign-in is finished by
`POST /auth/two-factor-challenge`. Public. Limited to 10 requests per minute per IP address, and
5 failed attempts per minute for one email address from one IP address.

put.description:
Send one `file` part (`multipart/form-data`): a JPEG, PNG or WebP of at most 5 MB, 8 000
pixels on a side and 40 million pixels. It is recognised by its content, re-encoded into
three WebP sizes (64, 160, 480 pixels), stripped of every piece of metadata, and the
upload itself is never kept. The previous logo's files are deleted once the new one is
stored. Owner only. Limited to 10 requests per hour per user.

delete.description:
The institution is shown with its initials again. Answers 204 whether or not there was a
logo. Owner only.

post.description:
Ends the session: it is destroyed in Redis and the CSRF token regenerated, so the old
session cookie opens nothing. Signed-in user.

get.description:
The user and their institution (`null` for a platform admin). The web application reads
it on every page of the admin area. A user whose institution was suspended since
sign-in is refused, and the session is ended. Signed-in user.

patch.description:
In this slice, the language of the admin area (`fr` or `en`). It also becomes the language of
the emails sent to this user from then on. Only the signed-in user's own row changes; any
other field of the body is ignored. Signed-in user.

get.description:
By name, ignoring case, then creation order, in any status of the election. An election
holds at most 30, so `per_page=100` returns them all. Owner or manager.
get.summary: List the parties of an election

post.description:
To a draft election, at most 30 per election (409 `party_limit_reached`). The name is
unique in the election, ignoring case. Owner or manager. Limited to 120 requests per hour per user.

patch.description:
Every field is optional; only those sent change. A draft election only. Owner or
manager. Limited to 120 requests per hour per user.

delete.description:
A draft election only. Final: there is no trash. Owner or manager. Limited to 120
requests per hour per user.

put.description:
Send one `file` part (`multipart/form-data`) under the rules of the election cover: JPEG,
PNG or WebP recognised by content, 5 MB, 8 000 pixels on a side, 40 million pixels, not
animated. Two WebP files are written, 96 and 192 pixels wide, ratio kept, never enlarged,
metadata dropped, the upload never kept; the previous logo's files are deleted afterwards.
A draft election only. Owner or manager. Limited to 20 requests per hour per user.
put.summary: Replace the logo of a party

delete.description:
Answers 204 whether or not there was a logo. A draft election only. Owner or manager.
Limited to 120 requests per hour per user.
delete.summary: Remove the logo of a party

get.description:
No sign-in, no cookie. Its name, type, logo, description and city, and its `published` elections (at most
50, newest publication first). No address, phone, email, user, voter or count. An unknown institution, a
value that is not a UUID and a suspended institution answer the same 404. Limited to 120 requests per
minute per address. `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
get.summary: The public profile of an institution

get.description:
A PDF for anyone, following the election's `results_display`: a `winners` election's report has no counts
and no bulletin check line. Any status but `published`, an unknown election, a value that is not a UUID and
a suspended institution answer the same 404. Generated on request. Limited to 30 requests per minute per
address and election.
get.summary: The results report of a published election

200.description: The PDF report, as an attachment.

get.description:
No sign-in, no cookie. Only a `published` election of an institution that is not suspended; any other
status, an unknown election and a value that is not a UUID answer the same 404. With the `full` display:
votes and percentages per candidate and the blank votes; with `winners`: the turnout, the winners and the
tied candidates only. Never the bulletin check, a voter or a numeric key. Limited to 120 requests per
minute per address and election. `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
get.summary: The public results of a published election

post.description:
Makes the results of a closed election public. `results_display` (`full` or `winners`) replaces the
election's setting when given. The row is locked, the status read again under the lock and the bulletin
check computed in the same transaction: 409 `results_check_failed` (`error.ballots`) when a ballot's
papers differ from its voters, 409 `election_not_closed` for any other status. A tie does not block it.
Owner or manager. Limited to 20 requests per hour per user, shared with unpublish, archive and unarchive.

A published election goes back to closed and `published_at` is cleared; the public pages answer 404 at
once. 409 `election_not_published` for any other status. Owner or manager. Limited as publish.

A closed or published election becomes archived (read-only, hidden from the default list) and `archived_at`
is set; an archived election is not public. 409 `election_not_archivable` for any other status. Owner or
manager. Limited as publish.

An archived election goes back to closed; `archived_at` and `published_at` are cleared (it is published
again on purpose). 409 `election_not_archived` for any other status. Owner or manager. Limited as publish.

Creates the institution and its first user, the owner, in one step, queues the
verification email and signs the owner in. Public. Limited to 10 requests per hour
per IP address.
post.summary: Register an institution and its owner

get.description:
The official results of a closed, published or archived election as a US Letter PDF, always with the full
counts and the bulletin check, in the election's language (409 `results_not_available` for any earlier
status). Generated on request, never stored. Owner or manager. Limited to 20 requests per hour per user.

200.description: The PDF report, as an attachment.

post.description:
Sends a new verification email to the signed-in user; the previous link stops working.
Signed-in user. Limited to 3 requests per minute per user.

Sets a new password with the token of the reset link. The user is not signed in, and
their other sessions stop working. Public. Limited to 10 requests per hour per IP address.

put.description:
The public note shown with a ballot's result: trimmed, up to 1 000 characters, control
characters other than line breaks removed; `null` or empty clears it. Only for a closed,
published or archived election (409 `results_not_available`). Owner or manager. Limited to
60 requests per hour per user.
put.summary: Set or clear the note of a result

get.description:
Per ballot, in the election's order: the voters eligible and those who voted, the papers cast
(blank included), the blank ones, the candidates by votes then by the election's order with
their percentage of the papers cast (one decimal), the winners, the tie for the last seats
(never broken) and the bulletin check. Only for a closed, published or archived election:
409 `results_not_available` otherwise. Counted from the votes and their choices only; the
audit table is never read. Owner or manager.

post.description:
A new draft election from a ballot of a closed, published or archived election whose result
has a tie: that ballot with only the tied candidates and the seats left, the same groups and
voters (no code, no vote). Title "Second tour – …" ("Second round – …" for an English
election), cut to 200 characters. 409 `ballot_not_tied`, `second_round_exists`,
`results_not_available`; 422 `ballot: invalid`. `parent` is the first election's UUID, in
this response only. Owner or manager. Limited to 20 requests per hour per user.

get.description:
How many voters have voted, in total, by group and over time, in any status. `bucket` is
`hour` or `day` (default: hour for an election of up to 3 days, else day); the series runs in
the election's time zone, empty buckets listed, empty while nobody has voted. Computed from
the participations only: never a vote, never what was voted. Owner or manager.

`enabled`: confirmed and asked at sign-in. `setup_started`: a secret was issued and not
confirmed. `recovery_codes_left`: how many unused recovery codes remain, `null` when not
enabled. Neither the secret nor a code is returned. Signed-in user.
get.summary: The state of the signed-in user's two-factor authentication

post.description:
Issues a new secret (a setup not yet confirmed is replaced) after the password is checked.
Not active until confirmed. The answer holds the secret and the `otpauth` link; the web
page draws the QR code in the browser. Signed-in user. Limited to 10 requests per minute
per user, shared with confirm, disable and recovery codes.

Confirms the setup with a first code from the authenticator application (6 digits; the
previous and the next period are accepted; a period already used is not) and returns
the eight recovery codes, shown only here and in the renewal. Open sessions stay open. A
wrong code does not end the setup. Signed-in user. Limited to 10 requests per minute per
user, shared with setup, disable and recovery codes.

Clears the secret, the recovery codes, the confirmation time and the stored period after
the password and a current second factor (`code`, or `recovery_code`, checked first when
both are sent) are checked. A setup that was never confirmed counts as not turned on.
Signed-in user. Limited to 10 requests per minute per user, shared with setup, confirm and
recovery codes.

Replaces the recovery codes with eight new ones after the password and a current second
factor (`code`, or `recovery_code`, checked first when both are sent) are checked; the old
ones stop working. Shown only here. Signed-in user. Limited to 10 requests per minute per
user, shared with setup, confirm and disable.

The second step of signing in for a person who has two-factor authentication turned on:
one `code` from the authenticator application (6 digits; the previous and the next
30-second period are accepted, a period already used is not) or one `recovery_code`
(checked first when both are sent; used up by a success). It only ever finishes the
sign-in that the password step recorded in this browser's session, for five minutes;
five wrong codes end it. Five wrong codes in 15 minutes for one account, from any browser or
address, answer 429 even for a right code. The session id is regenerated. Public. Limited to 10 requests
per minute per IP address.
post.summary: Finish signing in with a code

get.description:
Owners first, then managers, each by name (case and accents ignored), then by email. A
removed user is not listed. Owner only.

post.description:
For a person who has lost both their device and their recovery codes: the secret, the
recovery codes, the confirmation time and the stored period are cleared; their open
sessions stay open and their next sign-in asks for the password only. The owner's own
password is asked: a wrong one is a 422, and the fifth in 15 minutes ends the owner's
session (401). An owner who has two-factor on also gives a current `code` or `recovery_code`
(a wrong one is a 422, counted with the wrong codes at sign-in; the sixth is a 429). Not for oneself (the page "Mon compte" asks for the password). Owner only.
Limited to 10 requests per minute per user, shared with the own-settings routes.
post.summary: Turn off another user's two-factor authentication

post.description:
Verifies the address with the token of the link sent by email. The person may open the
link in another browser than the one they registered with, so no session is needed and
nobody is signed in by it. Public. Limited to 10 requests per minute per IP address.

get.description:
Only the ballots the voter is eligible for (the general ones and those of their group), each
with its candidates, party, photo and slogan, in the election's order; a `shuffled` order is
fixed for the session. The voter has no id here: the session names them. 401
`voter_session_expired` without a live session of this election; 409 `already_voted` for a
session that voted or a voter who has a participation; 409 `election_not_open` when the election is not open now.
get.summary: The voter's name and group, and the ballots they may fill

get.description:
The election, its period and whether it can be voted in now (`phase`: `before`, `open` or
`closed`, from the status and the server's clock, never the device's). `results` is the
path of the public results page once the election is published and its institution is not suspended. A draft, an unknown election
and a value that is not a UUID all answer 404. No session; no count; no ballot. Limited per
address and election.
get.summary: What a voter may know before entering a code

post.description:
The code (any case, with or without the hyphen, spaces ignored) is hashed with the credential
key and looked up in this election only; an unknown, wrong, another election's, malformed or
replaced code answers the same 401 `invalid_code`, after the same work. A valid code opens a
session: a random token in the `vote_session` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, path
`/api/v1/vote`), kept at most 15 minutes; a session the browser already had is replaced.
Only wrong codes are counted: 30 in 10 minutes per address (an IPv6 client by its /64) and election, 300 in an hour per
election, 429 with `Retry-After` (a locked-out address is refused even with a valid code; the election
limit refuses wrong codes only). A voter has one live session: a new one ends the earlier one.
409 `already_voted`, then 409 `election_not_open` with its `phase`.
post.summary: Enter a code and open a voter session

delete.description:
"Not me", "next voter" or leaving: the session is forgotten and the cookie cleared. No
session, an expired one or another election's session is nothing to end, and answers the
same 204. A vote or a participation never changes.

post.description:
Every ballot the voter is eligible for, together, once, in one transaction with the voter's
row locked: the election is open (status and server time), there is no participation yet, the
ballots are exactly the eligible ones (422 `ballots_mismatch`) and each ballot's choices
break no rule (422 `choices_invalid`); then the participation, one paper per ballot, its
choices and its sealed audit record are written, or nothing is. The same submission sent
again in the same session answers 200 with the same time and writes nothing. The choices are
never returned and never logged. 10 requests per minute per session.

get.description:
24 per page by default, by full name ignoring case, then creation order, in any status of
the election. `q` looks for a text in the full name, the identifier and the email; `group`
is a group's UUID or `none`; `credential` is `issued` or `none`; `email` is the status of
the last email (`queued`, `sent`, `failed`, `none`); `voted` is `yes` or `no`. Owner or manager.
get.summary: List the voters of an election

parameters.name: credential
parameters.description: Slice 11: the credential and the last email of the voter.

post.description:
To a draft, scheduled or open election, at most 10 000 per election (409
`voter_limit_reached`). `group` is a group's name: the group is found, or created
(409 `group_limit_reached` at 100; an open election takes existing groups only,
409 `election_voters_locked`). The identifier and the email are unique in the election.
Owner or manager. Limited to 240 requests per hour per user.

patch.description:
Every field is optional; only those sent change. `null` or blank clears the group, the
identifier, the email and the phone. A draft, scheduled or open election; an open one
keeps the voter's group (409 `election_voters_locked`). Owner or manager.
Limited to 240 requests per hour per user.

delete.description:
A draft or scheduled election only: slice 12 knows who has voted in an open one. Final:
there is no trash. The voter's group stays. Owner or manager. Limited to 240 requests per
hour per user.

post.description:
Copies the voters of `source`, another election of the institution in any status, into this
draft or scheduled election, with their groups (found by name or created; `rename` gives a
group another name). `groups` limits the copy to some groups of the source and
`include_ungrouped` says whether the voters with no group come too. A voter whose identifier
or email the election already has is skipped and counted. Credentials, codes and dates are
never copied. One transaction; a 409 leaves the election as it was. Owner or manager.
Limited to 20 requests per hour per user.
post.summary: Load the voters of another election

post.description:
The first code, or a new one that replaces a lost slip (the old one no longer matches any
voter, `reissue_count` goes up). The code is in the answer once, with a ready one-slip file
and the voter; the answer is never cached. A draft, scheduled or open election (409
`election_codes_locked`); a file that cannot be written gives a 500 and keeps the old code.
With `email` true the new code is also emailed to the voter in the background (`email`
`queued` in the answer; 422 `email: no_address` for a voter with no address, and nothing
changes; 403 `email_not_verified`; 409 `email_quota_exceeded`). Owner or manager. Limited to 60 requests per hour per user.

get.description:
An Excel or CSV file of the voters of an election, written as a stream: full name, group,
identifier, email, phone, and `has voted` for `voted=all`. `voted` is `no` (default), `yes`
or `all`; `group` is a group's UUID or `none`; `q` searches as in the list. Sorted by group
name then full name, the voters with no group last. Never a code, a hash, a link or a time of
vote; every text cell is guarded against formulas. Owner or manager. Limited to 20 requests
per hour per user.

An `.xlsx` (default, with an `Instructions` sheet in the signed-in user's language) or a
`.csv` (UTF-8 with a byte-order mark). The header `nom_complet`, `groupe`, `identifiant`,
`courriel`, `telephone` and three example rows; never a formula. An election in any
status. Owner or manager. Limited to 240 requests per hour per user.

post.description:
`multipart/form-data` with `file`: an `.xlsx` or a `.csv`, judged by its content, 5 MB at
most. A draft or scheduled election only. Nothing is imported: the file is checked in the
background (status `uploaded`, then `checked` or `failed`). One import at a time; a new
upload deletes the earlier `checked` and `failed` ones. Owner or manager. Limited to 20
uploads per hour per user.

get.description:
Its status, its summary and its progress. Any status. Owner or manager. Limited to 240
requests per hour per user.

patch.description:
Body `mapping`: an object of voter fields to a column index or `null`; a key left out
keeps its value. A `checked` import of a draft or scheduled election; it is checked
again in the background (202, status `uploaded`). Owner or manager. Limited to 240
requests per hour per user.

delete.description:
Its file and its rows are deleted; the voters already written stay. Any status except
`importing` (409 `import_in_progress`); an `uploaded` import is cancelled and the check
ends without writing. Owner or manager. Limited to 240 requests per hour per user.

get.description:
50 a page, in file order; `filter` is `all`, `ok` or `errors` (every invalid row,
duplicates included). An `uploaded` or `failed` import has no rows (409
`import_not_checked`). Owner or manager. Limited to 240 requests per hour per user.
get.summary: List the rows of a checked import

post.description:
The valid rows are written in the background, in chunks of 500, each one in a transaction
that locks the election first; the duplicates are judged again against the voters that
exist then. Answers 202 with the import (status `importing`); poll the import for the
progress. A draft or scheduled election (409 `election_voters_locked`), a `checked` import
(409 `import_not_checked`), at least one valid row (409 `nothing_to_import`), at most
10 000 voters in all (409 `voter_limit_reached`). Owner or manager. Limited to 240 requests
per hour per user.

get.description:
An `.xlsx` with the template columns, then `ligne` (the line in the uploaded file) and
`raison` (the reasons in words, in the signed-in user's language); the values are the
original cells, and a text beginning with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is prefixed with `'`. A
`checked` or `done` import with rejected rows (409 `no_error_file`). Owner or manager.
Limited to 240 requests per hour per user.

AcceptInvitationRequest.description:
docs/api/auth/POST-auth-accept-invitation.md. Only the token is judged here: the rest of
the body is judged after the token has been found (an unknown token answers 404 before any
422, so a bad body never reveals whether a token is valid).
AcceptInvitationRequest.title: AcceptInvitationRequest

CloseElectionRequest.description:
docs/api/elections/POST-elections-{election}-close.md: the typed confirmation. That it equals the title
is judged in the controller, under the row lock, after the status.
CloseElectionRequest.title: CloseElectionRequest

email.description: `max` before `email`: an address that is far too long is told "too long".

DuplicateElectionRequest.description: docs/api/elections/POST-elections-{election}-duplicate.md: an optional title, and whether to copy the candidates.
DuplicateElectionRequest.title: DuplicateElectionRequest

ExtendElectionRequest.description:
docs/api/elections/POST-elections-{election}-extend.md: `ends_at` is required and an ISO 8601 date and time.
Its place against the current end is judged in the controller, under the row lock.
ExtendElectionRequest.title: ExtendElectionRequest

PasswordRequest.description: The password of the signed-in user, asked again to change the second factor.
PasswordRequest.title: PasswordRequest

PreviewCredentialRunRequest.description: docs/api/credentials/POST-elections-{election}-credential-previews.md: the scope and group of a run.
PreviewCredentialRunRequest.title: PreviewCredentialRunRequest

PublishElectionRequest.description:
docs/api/publication/POST-elections-{election}-publish.md: the optional display choice. A plain `in` rule on
purpose: the shared renderer answers it as `results_display: invalid`.
PublishElectionRequest.title: PublishElectionRequest

ResetTwoFactorRequest.description:
The owner's password, and the owner's own second factor when the owner has two-factor on and
the user named is somebody else (a reset of oneself is refused with 409 after the password).
ResetTwoFactorRequest.title: ResetTwoFactorRequest

ResultNoteRequest.description:
docs/api/results/PUT-ballots-{ballot}-result-note.md: `note` is a string or null. It is trimmed, its
control characters other than line breaks are removed, and empty clears it; at most 1 000 characters.
ResultNoteRequest.title: ResultNoteRequest

SecondFactorRequest.description:
The password and a current second factor (`code` or `recovery_code`), asked to turn
two-factor off and to renew the recovery codes. Only the presence of the second factor is
judged here: anything that is not a right value (a short code, a list, a long text) is answered
`invalid` by the action, and counted.
SecondFactorRequest.title: SecondFactorRequest

SecondRoundRequest.title: SecondRoundRequest

TwoFactorCodeRequest.description:
The code of the authenticator application that confirms a setup. Only its presence is judged
here: anything that is not exactly 6 digits (a number, a list, a long text) is answered
`code: invalid` by the controller.
TwoFactorCodeRequest.title: TwoFactorCodeRequest

UpdateBallotRequest.description: docs/api/ballots/PATCH-ballots-{ballot}.md: the rules of the creation, every field optional.
UpdateBallotRequest.title: UpdateBallotRequest

UpdateCandidateRequest.description: docs/api/candidates/PATCH-candidates-{candidate}.md: the rules of the creation, every field optional, and `ballot`.
UpdateCandidateRequest.title: UpdateCandidateRequest

UpdateElectionRequest.description:
docs/api/elections/PATCH-elections-{election}.md: every field is optional; the order of the
dates is judged on the values as they will be after the change.
UpdateElectionRequest.title: UpdateElectionRequest

UpdateGroupRequest.description: docs/api/groups/PATCH-groups-{group}.md: the rules of the creation; the group's own name is no duplicate.
UpdateGroupRequest.title: UpdateGroupRequest

UpdateInstitutionRequest.description: docs/api/institution/PATCH-institution.md: every field is optional, only those sent change.
UpdateInstitutionRequest.title: UpdateInstitutionRequest

UpdatePartyRequest.description: docs/api/parties/PATCH-parties-{party}.md: the rules of the creation, every field optional.
UpdatePartyRequest.title: UpdatePartyRequest

UpdateVoterRequest.description: docs/api/voters/PATCH-voters-{voter}.md: the rules of the creation, every field optional.
UpdateVoterRequest.title: UpdateVoterRequest
